html:
The Wudjari are a Noongar people of the south coast of Western Australia, around present-day Esperance. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Goreng and Minang to the west, the Ngadjumaya to the east and the Kalaako and Malpa inland. French ships of the d'Entrecasteaux expedition sheltered at Esperance Bay in 1792 and named it after one of their vessels. In 1841 Edward John Eyre, near the end of his crossing from Adelaide, was helped by a French whaling ship anchored on their coast. The Dempster brothers took up land for sheep at Esperance in the 1860s.
